bull.t: Very high gross margins and operating profitability
bull.b: Sustained extremely high gross margins and healthy operating margins reflect Arm's IP‑centric business model with minimal manufacturing cost. That structural margin advantage supports durable cash generation, reinvestment in R&D and ecosystem growth, and resilience across semiconductor cycles.

bull.t: Strong cash generation and very low leverage
bull.b: Consistently strong operating and free cash flow combined with minimal debt give Arm durable financial flexibility to fund R&D, secure manufacturing commitments, and absorb cyclical downturns. Low leverage reduces refinancing risk and enables strategic investments without stressing the balance sheet.

Rapid adoption across cloud and infrastructure (explosive data-center royalty growth, major partner wins, and AGI CPU demand >$2B) signals a structural shift toward Arm architectures in AI compute. That expands long-term royalty runway and widens competitive moats via software and developer ecosystem effects.

bear.b: Arm's royalty model ties revenue to device volumes; sustained handset softness and higher BOMs can meaningfully temper royalty growth. Until handset demand stabilizes or other end markets absorb growth, revenue cyclicality and royalty growth moderation remain a structural headwind.

bear.t: Supply-chain constraints could limit AGI CPU scaling
bear.b: Scaling silicon-based revenue from the AGI CPU depends on foundry and component capacity. Structural shortages in wafers, substrates, test and memory can delay shipment ramp and postpone royalty and silicon revenue realization, compressing expected multi-year upside until supply expands.

bear.t: Initial AGI CPU margin headwinds and elevated R&D/OpEx
bear.b: First-generation AGI silicon starting with mid-to-high 30s margins plus rising R&D/OpEx implies several quarters of diluted consolidated margins. The multi-year margin improvement path requires time and scale; meanwhile elevated investment pressures near-term profitability and cash conversion metrics.
